name: Fix a node with no CNI config
objective: CKA › Services & Networking + Troubleshooting. Drill the whole pod-networking surface harder than the exam: how the CNI hands out pod IPs from the pod CIDR, the node-level CNI config, a no-hint diagnose-and-fix for a broken CNI, CoreDNS resolution, ClusterIP + endpoints, the full pod→Service datapath, headless Services, and NodePort. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a node with no CNI config
questions.teach:
When a node's CNI config under `/etc/cni/net.d/` is gone, the kubelet can't attach new pods there and they hang with no IP — and the kubelet says exactly that: `docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e | grep -i cni` shows `cni config uninitialized` / `NetworkPluginNotReady`. The kindnet DaemonSet **rewrites that config every time its pod starts**, so bouncing kindnet on the bad node restores it.

**Gotcha:** target just the broken node with `--field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2` — don't delete the whole DaemonSet.
questions.prompt:
Pod `netbroken` (pinned to node `$W2`) is stuck with no IP — new pods on `$W2` aren't getting networking. Diagnose the fault on `$W2` and repair it so `netbroken` gets an IP. Don't delete `netbroken`; fix the node.

Target: `netbroken` has a `.status.podIP`.
questions.hint: Compare `$W2` to a healthy node: `docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d` — the kindnet conflist is missing (and `docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e | grep -i cni` shows `cni config uninitialized`). Make kindnet rewrite it by restarting its pod on that node: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l app=kindnet --field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2`. Wait ~15s.
questions.solution:
docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d   # empty: the CNI config is gone
docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e | grep -i cni | tail   # 'cni config uninitialized'
kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l app=kindnet --field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2
# the new kindnet pod rewrites /etc/cni/net.d/10-kindnet.conflist; netbroken then gets an IP
kubectl get pod netbroken -n cni-learn -o wide

verification.description: CNI restored on $W2 — netbroken now has an IP in the pod CIDR

questions.eli5:
Remember the sticky note by the phone that tells a node which networking utility company to call? On node `$W2`, somebody tore that note off the wall. The node still works, but when a new pod shows up, the kubelet reaches for the instructions, finds nothing, and can't wire the pod up. So `netbroken` sits there with **no IP**, stuck forever.

This is a **diagnose-then-fix** drill, like being a detective. You don't get told the cause — you have to find it.

**Step 1 — compare to a healthy node.** Look in `/etc/cni/net.d/` on the broken node: `docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d`. It's **empty**, while a healthy node has `10-kindnet.conflist`. That's your smoking gun.

**Step 2 — confirm from the kubelet's own mouth.** `docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e | grep -i cni` shows it complaining: `cni config uninitialized` / `NetworkPluginNotReady`. The kubelet is literally telling you the CNI config is missing.

**Step 3 — fix it the clever way.** Here's the trick: the **kindnet DaemonSet rewrites that config file every time its pod starts up**. So you don't manually recreate the file — you just **restart kindnet's pod on that one node**, and it regenerates the note for you. Delete only the kindnet pod on `$W2`, wait ~15 seconds for the replacement to come up, and `netbroken` gets its IP.

**Watch out for:**

- **Target only the broken node.** Use `--field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2` so you delete just that node's kindnet pod. Do **not** delete the whole DaemonSet or every kindnet pod — you'd break networking cluster-wide.
- **Don't delete `netbroken` itself.** The task is to fix the node; the pod picks up an IP once the CNI is healthy again.
- The fix isn't instant — give the new kindnet pod a few seconds to start and rewrite the config before checking.
- A missing *binary* in `/opt/cni/bin` would look similar but wouldn't be fixed by this — here it's the **config file** that's gone, which kindnet restores on restart.
questions.deepDive:
## Diagnose & fix: a node with no CNI config — full rundown

### The one-sentence model
If a node's CNI config in **`/etc/cni/net.d/`** is missing, the kubelet reports **`NetworkPluginNotReady` / `cni config uninitialized`** and cannot network new pods — they stick with **no IP** in `ContainerCreating`. Because the **kindnet DaemonSet rewrites the config on pod start**, restarting kindnet's pod *on that node* restores it.

### Symptom → where to look
| Symptom | Check | Expectation on a healthy node |
|---|---|---|
| Pod stuck, no `.status.podIP` | `kubectl get pod netbroken -o wide` | an IP in `10.244.0.0/16` |
| kubelet complaining | `docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e \| grep -i cni` | no `uninitialized` errors |
| CNI config | `docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d` | `10-kindnet.conflist` present |
| CNI binaries | `docker exec $W2 ls /opt/cni/bin` | plugin binaries present |
| kindnet running there | `kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l app=kindnet -o wide` | one Running pod on `$W2` |

### Diagnosis workflow
```bash
# 1) the stuck pod has no IP
kubectl get pod netbroken -n cni-learn -o wide

# 2) describe shows the reason
kubectl describe pod netbroken -n cni-learn | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
#   ... NetworkPluginNotReady / failed to set up sandbox: cni config uninitialized

# 3) compare the broken node to a healthy one
docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d          # EMPTY  (broken)
docker exec $W1 ls /etc/cni/net.d          # 10-kindnet.conflist  (healthy)

# 4) confirm from the kubelet journal
docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e | grep -i cni | tail
#   "cni config uninitialized" / "NetworkPluginNotReady"
```

### The fix (restart kindnet on the broken node only)
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l app=kindnet \
  --field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2
# DaemonSet controller recreates the pod; on start it writes
# /etc/cni/net.d/10-kindnet.conflist, and the kubelet can now attach pods.
```
Then wait and verify:
```bash
docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d                      # 10-kindnet.conflist back
kubectl get pod netbroken -n cni-learn -o wide         # now has a 10.244.x.y IP
```

### Why the `--field-selector` matters
`-l app=kindnet` alone matches **every** kindnet pod cluster-wide — deleting all of them would churn networking on every node. `--field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2` scopes the delete to the **one** pod on the broken node. Never `delete ds kindnet` (that removes the plugin entirely).

### General CNI-outage triage (exam toolkit)
| Cause | Signature | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Missing config file | `/etc/cni/net.d` empty, `uninitialized` | restart CNI DaemonSet pod on that node |
| Missing CNI binary | config present but `failed to find plugin` | restore `/opt/cni/bin`, redeploy CNI |
| Shadowing file | stray `00-*.conf` sorts first | remove the stray file |
| CNI DaemonSet not scheduled | no CNI pod on the node (taint/selector) | fix tolerations/nodeSelector |
| Node not Ready (CNI) | `kubectl get nodes` NotReady + CNI errors | fix CNI, kubelet reports Ready |

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Scope the delete** with `--field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2`; don't nuke the whole DaemonSet or all kindnet pods.
- **Don't delete the stuck pod** — fix the node; the pod gets an IP once CNI is healthy (it retries the sandbox).
- The fix is **not instant** — allow ~15s for the replacement kindnet pod to start and rewrite the config.
- Distinguish **missing config** (restored by restarting kindnet) from **missing binary** (`/opt/cni/bin`, not restored by a pod restart).
- On `kind`, node internals are reached via **`docker exec <node>`**, not `kubectl` — the config lives on the node filesystem.
- A `NotReady` node with `KubeletNotReady … cni config uninitialized` is the same root cause at the node level.

### Quick reference
```bash
docker exec $W2 ls /etc/cni/net.d                         # empty = cause found
docker exec $W2 journalctl -u kubelet -e | grep -i cni    # cni config uninitialized
kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l app=kindnet \
  --field-selector spec.nodeName=$W2                      # restart kindnet on $W2
kubectl get pod netbroken -n cni-learn -o wide            # IP appears
```
